prompt: Which of these elements exists naturally as two-atom (diatomic) molecules?

choices.why: Sulfur normally exists as an eight-atom molecule, S8.
One form of phosphorus exists as a four-atom molecule, P4.
Neon isn't one of the elements that form molecules, so it is treated as individual atoms.

explanation: Seven elements exist as diatomic molecules: hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine. So bromine's molecular formula is Br2.

prompt: What is the name of PCl5?

choices.why: Don't use mono- when there is only one atom of the first element.
A prefix loses its a or o only before an element name that begins with o, as in pentoxide. Chloride keeps the full penta-.
The second element is named with its stem plus -ide: chlor + -ide = chloride.

explanation: One phosphorus atom gets no prefix, since mono- is never used on the first element. Five chlorine atoms make penta- + chlor + -ide: pentachloride.

prompt: What is the name of N2O?

choices.why: When a prefix ends in o and the element name begins with o, the prefix's o is dropped: monoxide.
The second element always gets a numerical prefix, even mono- for one atom. Only the first element skips mono-.
That name means one nitrogen atom: NO. N2O has two, so the first element needs di-.

explanation: Two nitrogen atoms make dinitrogen. One oxygen atom makes mono- + ox + -ide, with the o of mono- dropped before oxide: monoxide.

prompt: What is the formula of dichlorine heptoxide?

choices.why: Di- on chlorine means two chlorine atoms, so chlorine needs a subscript 2.
Hepta- means seven; hexa- is six.
Each prefix belongs to the element it is attached to: di- (2) goes with chlorine, hepta- (7) with oxygen.

explanation: Di- means two chlorine atoms, and hepta- means seven oxygen atoms (the a of hepta- is dropped before oxide). List the symbols in the order of the name: Cl2O7.

prompt: How many atoms in all are in one molecule of sulfur hexafluoride?
explanation: Sulfur has no prefix, so there is one sulfur atom (mono- is never used on the first element), and hexa- means six fluorine atoms. SF6 has 1 + 6 = 7 atoms.

prompt: How many atoms in all are in one molecule of tetraphosphorus decoxide?
explanation: Tetra- means four phosphorus atoms, and deca- means ten oxygen atoms (the a of deca- is dropped before oxide). P4O10 has 4 + 10 = 14 atoms.

prompt: Which description fits a molecule?

choices.text: two or more atoms connected so they behave as one particle
a single atom that behaves as an independent particle
choices.why: A molecule is composed of more than one atom, so a single atom is not a molecule.

choices.text: the connection that holds two atoms together in a group
choices.why: That connection is a chemical bond. The molecule is the whole group of connected atoms.

choices.text: a sample that contains two or more different substances
choices.why: That describes a mixture. The atoms in a molecule are connected into one particle.

explanation: A molecule is two or more atoms connected so strongly that they behave as a single particle. It is the smallest part of a substance that has the physical and chemical properties of that substance.

prompt: Carbon dioxide, CO2, is made of carbon and oxygen. What is the smallest part of carbon dioxide that still has the physical and chemical properties of carbon dioxide?

choices.why: A carbon atom alone is only part of a CO2 molecule, so it doesn't have the properties of carbon dioxide.
An oxygen atom alone is only part of a CO2 molecule, so it doesn't have the properties of carbon dioxide.
O2 is a molecule of elemental oxygen, a different substance. It contains no carbon.

explanation: A molecule is the smallest part of a substance that has the physical and chemical properties of that substance. For carbon dioxide, that is one CO2 molecule: one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms connected together.

prompt: What is a chemical bond?

choices.text: the connection between two atoms in a molecule
a group of atoms that behaves as a single particle
choices.why: That describes a molecule. A chemical bond is the connection between two of the atoms in it.

choices.text: the system of rules used to name compounds
choices.why: That is chemical nomenclature.

choices.text: a listing of what and how many atoms are in a molecule
choices.why: That is a molecular formula.

explanation: A chemical bond is the connection between two atoms in a molecule. In molecular art, where atoms are drawn as balls, a bond is drawn as a line connecting two balls.

prompt: What does a molecular formula tell you about a molecule?

choices.text: which kinds of atoms it contains and how many of each
how its atoms are arranged in space
choices.why: A molecular formula is only a listing of what and how many atoms are in a molecule. It doesn't show how they are arranged.

choices.text: which elements it contains, but not how many atoms of each
choices.why: The subscripts give the number of atoms of each element, and no subscript means one atom.

choices.text: how many molecules are in a sample of the substance
choices.why: A molecular formula describes a single molecule: the kinds and numbers of atoms in it.

explanation: A molecular formula is a formal listing of what and how many atoms are in a molecule. Each element's symbol is followed by a subscript for its number of atoms, and no subscript means one atom.

prompt: Which of these elements is treated as individual atoms rather than as molecules?

choices.why: Nitrogen exists naturally as diatomic molecules, N2.
Iodine exists naturally as diatomic molecules, I2.
Chlorine exists naturally as diatomic molecules, Cl2.

explanation: Nitrogen, iodine, and chlorine are among the elements that exist as diatomic molecules (N2, I2, Cl2). Elements that aren't known to form molecules, such as argon, are assumed to exist as individual atoms.

prompt: Elemental sulfur normally exists as molecules rather than as individual atoms. How many sulfur atoms are in one molecule of elemental sulfur?
explanation: Sulfur normally exists as an eight-atom molecule, so its molecular formula is S8.

prompt: Each of these formulas represents a molecule. Which one is a molecule of an element rather than of a compound?

choices.why: PCl3 contains two elements, phosphorus and chlorine, so it is a compound.
SiF4 contains two elements, silicon and fluorine, so it is a compound.
NF3 contains two elements, nitrogen and fluorine, so it is a compound.

explanation: P4 contains only phosphorus atoms, so it is a molecule of an element: one form of elemental phosphorus exists as four-atom P4 molecules. The other formulas each contain two different elements, so they are compounds.

prompt: Which pair of elements is most likely to combine into a compound that exists as molecules?

choices.why: Sodium is a metal. Compounds between a metal and a nonmetal are a different kind of compound; it is nonmetals connected with nonmetals that typically form molecules.
Calcium is a metal. Molecules typically form when a nonmetal connects with another nonmetal, not with a metal.
Both are metals. Molecules typically form when nonmetals connect with other nonmetals.

explanation: When nonmetals connect with other nonmetals, the compounds typically exist as molecules. Sulfur and fluorine are both nonmetals; each of the other pairs includes a metal.

prompt: Nitrogen and oxygen form several different molecules, including NO and NO2. Why does chemical nomenclature give each of them its own name?

choices.text: They are different compounds with different properties.
They contain different elements, so their names have to differ.
choices.why: Both contain only nitrogen and oxygen. They differ in the number of oxygen atoms, which the prefixes show.

choices.text: One of them is an element and the other is a compound.
choices.why: Both contain two elements, nitrogen and oxygen, so both are compounds.

choices.text: One of them is a molecule and the other is a set of separate atoms.
choices.why: Both are molecules. Compounds of nonmetals with other nonmetals typically exist as molecules.

explanation: Molecules made of the same elements in different numbers are different compounds with different chemical and physical properties. Nomenclature gives each compound a unique name, and each name refers to only one compound.

prompt: What is a binary compound?

choices.text: a compound made of exactly two different elements
a compound whose molecules each contain exactly two atoms
choices.why: Binary refers to two elements, not two atoms. N2O4 has six atoms but only two elements, so it is binary.

choices.text: an element whose molecules each contain two atoms
choices.why: That describes a diatomic element such as Cl2. An element is not a compound.

choices.text: a compound formed between a metal and a nonmetal
choices.why: Binary describes how many elements a compound has, not what kind they are. The binary compounds named with prefixes are made of nonmetals.

explanation: A binary compound has only two elements in it, such as nitrogen and fluorine in NF3. The number of atoms doesn't matter: a molecule with many atoms of just two elements is still binary.

prompt: Which numerical prefix indicates nine atoms of an element in the name of a molecule?

choices.why: Octa- means eight.
Deca- means ten.
Hepta- means seven.

explanation: The prefixes for 1 through 10 are mono-, di-, tri-, tetra-, penta-, hexa-, hepta-, octa-, nona-, and deca-. Nona- means nine.

prompt: A student names the molecule I2O5 "diiodine pentaoxide." How should the name be corrected?

choices.text: Drop the a of penta- before oxide: diiodine pentoxide
Drop one i where di- meets iodine: diodine pentaoxide
choices.why: Only a prefix ending in a or o loses that letter, and only before an element name beginning with o. Di- before iodine keeps both i's: diiodine.

choices.text: Remove di-, since the first element gets no prefix: iodine pentaoxide
choices.why: Only mono- is left off the first element. Two iodine atoms need di-.

choices.text: Leave it as is; diiodine pentaoxide is already correct
choices.why: When a prefix ends in a and the element name begins with o, the a is dropped, so pentaoxide becomes pentoxide.

explanation: Two iodine atoms make diiodine, and five oxygen atoms make penta- + ox + -ide. Because penta- ends in a and oxide begins with o, the a is dropped: diiodine pentoxide.

prompt: S4N4 and S2N2 are two different molecules. A student names both of them "sulfur nitride," reasoning that each has equal numbers of sulfur and nitrogen atoms. What is the problem with this?

choices.text: Both elements need prefixes: tetrasulfur tetranitride and disulfur dinitride.
Nothing is wrong; equal numbers of atoms cancel, so no prefixes are needed.
choices.why: Prefixes give the actual number of atoms of each element, not a ratio. Without them, two different compounds would share one name.

choices.text: Only nitrogen needs a prefix: sulfur tetranitride and sulfur dinitride.
choices.why: Only mono- is left off the first element. Four or two sulfur atoms need tetra- or di-.

choices.text: Use nitrogen, not nitride: tetrasulfur tetranitrogen and disulfur dinitrogen.
choices.why: The second element is named with its stem plus -ide: nitr + -ide = nitride.

explanation: Prefixes show how many atoms of each element are present, so that each compound gets its own name. S4N4 is tetrasulfur tetranitride, and S2N2 is disulfur dinitride.

prompt: When each of these prefixes comes right before oxide in a compound's name, which one keeps all of its letters?

choices.why: Mono- ends in o, so it loses the o before oxide: monoxide.
Tetra- ends in a, so it loses the a before oxide: tetroxide.
Octa- ends in a, so it loses the a before oxide: octoxide.

explanation: A prefix that ends in a or o drops that letter before an element name beginning with o. Di- ends in i, so it stays whole: dioxide. Mono-, tetra-, and octa- become monoxide, tetroxide, and octoxide.

prompt: Which of these molecules has a name that begins with a numerical prefix?

choices.why: NF3 has only one nitrogen atom, and mono- is never used on the first element, so its name begins with nitrogen.
SiCl4 has one silicon atom, which gets no prefix. The tetra- goes on the second element: silicon tetrachloride.
CS2 has one carbon atom, which gets no prefix. The di- goes on the second element: carbon disulfide.

explanation: The first element gets a prefix only when there is more than one atom of it. N2F4 has two nitrogen atoms, so its name begins with di-: dinitrogen tetrafluoride.

prompt: Which formula is paired with its correct name?

choices.why: Two nitrogen atoms need the prefix di-: dinitrogen trioxide.
The second element always gets a prefix. Two chlorine atoms make dichloride: sulfur dichloride.
Five fluorine atoms take penta-; hepta- means seven. The name is bromine pentafluoride.

explanation: PBr3 has one phosphorus atom, which gets no prefix, and three bromine atoms: tri- + brom + -ide. Its name is phosphorus tribromide.

prompt: Which of these molecules contains the greatest total number of atoms?

choices.why: IF7 has 1 + 7 = 8 atoms. Hepta- is the largest prefix here, but there is only one iodine atom.
XeF6 has 1 + 6 = 7 atoms.
CBr4 has 1 + 4 = 5 atoms.

explanation: Add the atoms given by both prefixes, counting one atom for an element with no prefix. Tetraphosphorus hexoxide, P4O6, has 4 + 6 = 10 atoms, more than any of the others.

prompt: A student writes the formula of phosphorus triiodide as P1I3. What is wrong with this formula?

choices.text: The subscript 1 is not written, so the formula should be PI3.
The 3 belongs on phosphorus, so the formula should be P3I.
choices.why: Tri- is attached to iodide, so the 3 belongs to iodine.

choices.text: Phosphorus exists as P4, so the formula should be P4I3.
choices.why: P4 is elemental phosphorus. In a compound, the number of phosphorus atoms comes from the name, and no prefix means one atom.

choices.text: Nothing is wrong, because every symbol needs a subscript.
choices.why: The subscript 1 is never written. A symbol with no subscript means one atom.

explanation: Phosphorus triiodide has one phosphorus atom and three iodine atoms. Because 1 is implied when there is no subscript, the formula is PI3.

prompt: Chlorine dioxide and dichlorine monoxide are different compounds of chlorine and oxygen. How do their molecules differ?

choices.text: chlorine dioxide: one Cl, two O; dichlorine monoxide: two Cl, one O
chlorine dioxide: two Cl, one O; dichlorine monoxide: one Cl, two O
choices.why: Each prefix belongs to the element it is attached to. In chlorine dioxide, di- is on oxide, so the two atoms are oxygen.

choices.text: chlorine dioxide: two Cl, two O; dichlorine monoxide: two Cl, one O
choices.why: Chlorine has no prefix in chlorine dioxide, which means one chlorine atom.

choices.text: chlorine dioxide: one Cl, two O; dichlorine monoxide: one Cl, one O
choices.why: Di- on chlorine in dichlorine monoxide means two chlorine atoms.

explanation: Each prefix gives the number of atoms of the element it is attached to, and an element with no prefix has one atom. Chlorine dioxide is ClO2, and dichlorine monoxide is Cl2O.

prompt: When you write the formula of a binary molecular compound from its name, in what order do you write the element symbols?

choices.text: in the same order as the elements appear in the name
in alphabetical order by element symbol
choices.why: The formula follows the name, not the alphabet: list the symbols in the order of the name.

choices.text: with the element that has more atoms written first
choices.why: The number of atoms doesn't set the order. Nitrogen trichloride has more chlorine atoms, yet its formula is NCl3.

choices.text: with the element that has fewer atoms written first
choices.why: The number of atoms doesn't set the order. The symbols follow the order of the name, whichever element has more atoms.

explanation: List the element symbols in the order of the name, adding a subscript for any element with more than one atom. For example, nitrogen trichloride is NCl3.

prompt: In one molecule of disulfur decafluoride, how many more fluorine atoms are there than sulfur atoms?
explanation: Di- means two sulfur atoms, and deca- means ten fluorine atoms, so the formula is S2F10. There are 10 − 2 = 8 more fluorine atoms than sulfur atoms.

prompt: Which name is used for H2O in the formal system of chemical nomenclature?

choices.why: This name follows the prefix rules, but H2O is one of the simple molecules whose common name is used instead: water.
This name would mean one hydrogen atom and two oxygen atoms. H2O goes by its common name, water.
This name leaves out the prefixes, and H2O goes by its common name, water.

explanation: Some simple molecules have common names that are part of the formal system of nomenclature. H2O is called water, not dihydrogen monoxide.

prompt: Which of these molecules is known by a common name that is part of the formal system of chemical nomenclature?

choices.why: BrF3 is named with the prefix rules: bromine trifluoride.
SeF6 is named with the prefix rules: selenium hexafluoride.
ICl is named with the prefix rules: iodine monochloride.

explanation: A few simple molecules have common names that are used instead of prefix names. NH3 is called ammonia.

prompt: How many atoms in all are in one molecule of methane?
explanation: Methane is the common name for CH4, which has one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms: 1 + 4 = 5 atoms.
